limitations: Synthetic finite poster/landscape/codec bursts on a shared local Docker host; not sustained throughput, production percentiles or paired speedups.
Native wall time includes input preparation, inference, result construction and private probe verification, not kernel-only or thread CPU time.
Initial timing-only detached results lack private vector verification; final-source experiments require it.
Response start is an application event, not proof of peer receipt; unknown phases remain null.
Cgroup memory includes the isolated HTTP child; shared-page charging may be lower than process RSS. Do not subtract independent peaks or replace earlier cold-memory sizing.
Production parity probes use Torch intra-op 1; capacity experiments use 8 with inter-op 16. They are not paired throughput comparisons.
No physical ARM, NVIDIA/Intel GPU capacity, hosted Windows/Actions orchestration or external client-address preservation claim.
Observers are trusted internal callbacks, disabled by default, expected to return promptly and be thread-safe; ordinary callback errors are isolated, not adversarial callbacks.
No full repository security audit or release is claimed.
next_item: Design cooperative cancellation between native micro-batches without abandoning active calls, permits/read locks or images; preserve coalesced live callers; replay target-host caller/batch pressure before changing limits.
